_note: Shared parity vectors for the Gomoku rules. The Python tests (ml/tests/test_parity.py) and the TypeScript engine tests use the SAME cases, so a rules drift between the Python training code and the web app's engine shows up as a test failure on one side. Coordinates are (x, y) with x = column 0..14 left-to-right, y = row 0..14 top-to-bottom. 'sequence' cases list moves in play order, Black first; the game must end (or not end) exactly as 'expected_winner' says, and must not end before the final move. 'placement' cases list stones placed directly on the board (no move order) and check the winner of that static position. 'expected_winner' is 'black', 'white', 'draw', or 'none' (game not over). All vectors were hand-computed; each winning line is spelled out in 'winning_line' where applicable.
